To deal with large amounts of unsolicited email ("spam" or "junk mail"), Thunderbird uses an adaptive filter. This "adaptive" filter requires training data, which comes from you marking received messages as legitimate (not spam) and which are spam. The filter then identifies new messages it thinks are spam and moves them to the Spam folder. 

{warning}It is important to choose a mail provider that does good spam protection on their server, because using Thunderbird alone is not sufficient to block modern spammers.{/warning}

{note}Note: Starting with version 145, all references in Thunderbird and documentation have changed from Junk to Spam.{/note}

__TOC__
=Overview=
Thunderbird's adaptive filter uses a Bayes algorithm with training data, based on messages you mark as spam and not spam. But using an algorithm (a formula) means a message previously marked as spam is not guaranteed to be automatically marked as spam in the future. Likewise, marking a message as not spam does not guarantee a similar message will not be marked as spam. Therefore:
 
* It is important that you do not delete spam messages, but instead '''mark''' them as spam so that training occurs.
* To guarantee that a message WILL be marked as spam, see [[#w_create-filters-manually|Create filters manually]].
* To guarantee that important messages WILL NOT be marked as spam, use [[#w_whitelisting|Whitelisting]].
* You must [[#_repeated-training|frequently train Thunderbird]], for Thunderbird to do a good job of identifying spam.

=Spam filter settings=
== Global spam settings ==
Spam filtering is enabled by default. And you can set global spam settings to tune what should happen to messages marked as spam. These settings will be used for all email accounts (although some settings can be overridden in the [[#w_per-account-settings|Per account settings]], as shown below).
# Click {menu ≡} > {menu Settings} > {menu Privacy & Security} 
# Scroll down to '''Spam'''. Adjust the settings as you see fit.
#;[[Image: TB115-account-settings-junk-settings]]

== Per account settings ==
The spam settings in the account settings for each of your email accounts will override similar settings in the [[#w_global-junk-settings|Global settings]] described above. 
* Click {menu ≡} > {menu Account Settings} > '''Your email address''' > {menu Spam Settings}
*;[[Image: tb115-email-account-settings-junk-settings]] 

=== How to turn off Thunderbird's adaptive filtering ===
* Untick ''Enable adaptive spam mail controls for this account''

===Whitelisting===
Under ''Do not automatically mark mail as spam if the sender is in'' you can select address books which will be used as a whitelist. Senders whose email address is in a whitelisted address book are exempt and will not be automatically marked as spam by Thunderbird. But you can still manually marking a message containing a whitelisted address as spam. 

'''It is recommended that you enable whitelisting to help ensure that messages from people you most care about will not be marked as spam.'''

=Training the spam filter=
In order for Thunderbird's spam filter to be effective, you must train it to recognize messages that you consider to be spam '''and''' messages that you consider to be '''not''' spam. If you do not do both, then the filter will not be very effective. 

Note also, it is important to mark messages as spam before deleting them. Just deleting a message doesn't train the filter. 

== Tell Thunderbird what IS spam ==
There are several ways of marking messages as spam:
* You can click on the little icon in the ''Spam'' column of the [[Getting Started with the Thunderbird main window (Supernova and newer)#w_7-message-list-pane|Message List Pane]]:
*;[[Image: TB115-thread-pane-junk-column|width=300]]
* You can also click the {button Spam} button on the [[Getting Started with the Thunderbird main window (Supernova and newer)#w_8-message-header-pane|Message Header Pane]]:
*;[[Image: TB115-message-pane-header-buttons-junk|width=500]]
* Or you can press {key J} on your keyboard to mark one or more selected messages as spam.
{note}Once you mark a message as spam, if you have configured your [[#w_global-junk-settings|Global junk settings]] or [[#w_per-account-settings|Per account settings]] to move junk email to a different folder, the email will disappear from the [[Getting Started with the Thunderbird main window (Supernova and newer)#w_7-message-list-pane|Message List Pane]] for the current folder. Don't worry, the email has moved to the folder you have configured for spam mail.{/note}
{note}Thunderbird's spam filter has been designed to learn from the training data which you provide. Marking more messages as '''Spam''' or '''Not Spam''' (see below) will improve the accuracy of your spam filter by adding more training data.{/note}

== Tell Thunderbird what IS NOT spam ==
Sometimes Thunderbird's spam filter might get it wrong and mark ''good'' messages as spam. Therefore, it is just as important to tell the filter which messages are ''not'' spam, especially on a new installation of Thunderbird.
{note}'''Note:''' You should frequently (daily or weekly) check your Spam folder for ''good'' messages wrongly marked as spam by Thunderbird and mark them as '''Not Spam'''. This will recover the good messages and improve the correctness of the filter for the future.{/note}
There are several ways of marking messages as '''Not Spam'''.
* Click on the {button Not Spam} button in the yellow spam notification below the message header in the [[Getting Started with the Thunderbird main window (Supernova and newer)#w_7-message-list-pane|Message List Pane]]:
*;[[Image: TB115-message-pane-junk-notification-not-junk]]
* Click on the red spam icon in the '''Spam''' column of the [[Getting Started with the Thunderbird main window (Supernova and newer)#w_7-message-list-pane|Message List Pane]] to toggle the spam status of a message:
*;[[Image: TB115-thread-pane-unmark-junk-column|width=300]]
* Or press {key Shift}+{key J} on your keyboard to mark one or more messages as '''Not Spam'''.
{note}Once you un-mark a message as spam, the email will disappear from the current folder. Don't worry, the email is still there! It will be in its original folder; the folder it was in before it was marked as spam.{/note}

== Repeated training ==
You should '''regularly''' train the filter by marking a number of '''good''' messages as not spam - messages in your Inbox ''and'' messages that have been filtered into other folders. In this case, you can only use the keyboard shortcut {key Shift}+{key J}, because the {button Not Spam} button appears only for messages that have already been marked as spam. Marking several messages per week will be sufficient, and you can select many messages and mark all of them at the same time. 

Unfortunately the user interface does not help you see whether a message has already been marked as "not spam".

= Other ways of blocking unwanted messages =
Thunderbird's adaptive spam filter is not an absolute barrier against messages from a specific address or specific types of messages. You can have stronger mechanisms to stop unwanted messages by using the following methods.

== Create filters manually ==
You can manually:
* [[Blocking a sender|Block some senders]].
* [[Organize Your Messages by Using Filters#w_create-a-new-filter|Create filters]] to block messages based on subject or other criteria.

== Use a Thunderbird supported external filter service ==
If your mail provider offer SpamAssassin, Bogofilter, DSPAM, POPFile or SpamPal, then you can use their external filter service to help classify email and block spam.
# Click {menu ≡} > {menu Account Settings} > '''Your Account''' > {menu Spam Settings}
# Enable the {pref Trust spam headers set by} option.
# Choose an external filter service in the drop-down menu.
#;[[Image:TB115-Trust_junk_mail_headers_set_by|width=400]]

== Use your mail provider's spam or filter features ==
Your mail provider may offer features for avoiding spam or blocking messages. 

Also, mail providers often use services which collect data from thousands or millions of users to provide superior spam filtering. Depending on your provider, you can assist in the collection process by moving spam messages to the Spam folder or by marking messages as spam using the mail provider's webmail.
